title: Finite type algebras with finite fibre at a minimal prime become finite after one localization
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $S$ is generated by finitely many elements as an $R$-algebra. Let $\mathfrak p$ be a minimal prime ideal of $R$ (a prime containing no strictly smaller prime). Suppose the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$ is finite. Then there is $g\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that $S_{\varphi(g)}$ is a finitely generated module over $R_g$ via the induced homomorphism $R_g\to S_{\varphi(g)}$, where the rings are localizations obtained by inverting the indicated elements [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $A=S\otimes_R k$. The fibre-prime bijection [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] identifies the primes of $A$ with precisely the primes of $S$ whose contraction is $\mathfrak p$, so $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is finite. If $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ generate $S$ over $R$, their images generate $A$ over $k$: expand each pure tensor using the polynomial expression for its $S$-factor, and sum. Thus [pqf-lem-finite-type-algebra-finite-spectrum] applies and makes $A$ a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, including when $A=0$.

source.place: Tag 02ML (lemma-generically-finite), first two sentences; Tag 0H8X (lemma-quasi-finite-above-p) and Tag 0ALW (lemma-finite-type-algebra-finite-nr-primes)

proof.text: Write $S_{\mathfrak p}$ for localization at the image of $R\setminus\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-localization-quotient], $A\cong S_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}$ compatibly with the generators. For each generator image $\bar x_i$, the powers $1,\bar x_i,\ldots,\bar x_i^d$, where $d=\dim_k A$, are linearly dependent. Choose a nonzero relation, take its largest nonzero coefficient and divide by that coefficient to obtain a monic polynomial of positive degree annihilating $\bar x_i$ (if $A=0$, use $X$). Lift its nonleading coefficients along the quotient $R_{\mathfrak p}\twoheadrightarrow k$ and keep leading coefficient $1$, obtaining a monic $P_i\in R_{\mathfrak p}[X]$ with $P_i(x_i)\in\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 02ML (lemma-generically-finite), construction of the monic polynomials

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field], every element of $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ is nilpotent; here only minimality of $\mathfrak p$ is required, not reducedness of $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-nilpotent-extension] to $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak p}$ and this ideal. Its extension is $\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak p}$, since both ideals are generated by the images of the elements of $\mathfrak p$. Consequently for each $i$ there is $e_i\ge1$ such that $P_i(x_i)^{e_i}=0$ in $S_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 02ML (lemma-generically-finite), nilpotence paragraph using Tags 00EU and 0544

proof.text: Write all finitely many coefficients of the $P_i$ as fractions $a/b$ in $R_{\mathfrak p}$ with $b\notin\mathfrak p$. Let $g_1$ be their denominator product (empty product $1$). Primality gives $g_1\notin\mathfrak p$, and each $b$ is invertible in $R_{g_1}$, with inverse $(g_1/b)/g_1$, where $g_1/b$ means the product of all the other denominator factors. Replacing each coefficient by its resulting fraction defines monic $\widetilde P_i\in R_{g_1}[X]$ mapping to $P_i$. Set $r_i=\widetilde P_i(x_i)^{e_i}\in S_{\varphi(g_1)}$. Its image in $S_{\mathfrak p}$ is zero. The fraction equality criterion for localization at $R\setminus\mathfrak p$ gives $u_i\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $\varphi(u_i)r_i=0$ in $S_{\varphi(g_1)}$: equivalently write $r_i=s_i/\varphi(g_1)^{a_i}$ and use an element outside $\mathfrak p$ annihilating $s_i$.

source.place: Tag 02ML (lemma-generically-finite), choosing g_1 and g_2; localization fraction equality

proof.text: Let $g_2=\prod_i u_i$ (empty product $1$) and $g=g_1g_2$. Again $g\notin\mathfrak p$. Each $g_1$ and $u_i$ becomes invertible in $R_g$ and its image becomes invertible in $S_{\varphi(g)}$: for any factor $v$ of $g$, the inverse is the product of the other factors divided by $g$. The equalities $\varphi(u_i)r_i=0$ therefore imply $\widetilde P_i(x_i)^{e_i}=0$ in $S_{\varphi(g)}$. Thus $Q_i=\widetilde P_i^{e_i}$ is a monic polynomial of positive degree $D_i$ over $R_g$ annihilating $x_i$.

Every element of $S_{\varphi(g)}$ is $s/\varphi(g)^a$; expressing $s$ as a polynomial in the $x_i$ shows that the same generators generate this localization as an $R_g$-algebra. For each $i$, the monic equation $Q_i(x_i)=0$ expresses $x_i^{D_i}$ as an $R_g$-linear combination of lower powers of $x_i$. Repeated substitution decreases the exponent of that variable, so every monomial is an $R_g$-linear combination of $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}$ with $0\le a_i<D_i$. This finite set spans $S_{\varphi(g)}$ over $R_g$. For $n=0$ the set consists of the empty monomial $1$. This proves the claimed module finiteness.

source.place: Tag 02ML (lemma-generically-finite), final sentence expanded as a monomial spanning argument
